transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Elena Park (Redwood CSM); Aisha Grant (CISO, Sentinel Health), Mark DeLuca (CTO), Ravi Shah (Security PM), Jenna Ortiz (Cloud Engineer)

Summary:
Quick posture review covering SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts, Trust Center access, controls mapping, RBAC/SSO integration, audit log retention and SIEM ingestion, encryption and KMS patterns, and data residency options (Dedicated vs Hosted implications). Agreed next steps: share reports via Trust Center, deliver controls mapping spreadsheet, schedule KMS deep-dive.

Topics:
- Reports & Trust Center access
- Controls mapping (Redwood -> Sentinel)
- Identity & access (SSO/SAML, RBAC, service accounts)
- Audit logs, retention, SIEM / Splunk integration
- Encryption at rest & KMS/HSM options, BYOK
- Data residency & Dedicated/Private deployment options
- Evidence redaction & audit process

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time on a Friday. quick intros - i'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me priya and sam, our security/infra engineers.
[00:22] Aisha: Hi, Aisha here, CISO at Sentinel, we'll also have mark and ravi on the call. we're mainly looking to validate compliance posture for our procurement and internal audit.
[00:32] Priya: Awesome, thanks Aisha. today we'll run through our SOC 2 and ISO artifacts, how to get to the trust center, controls mapping, and then deep dive on encryption/KMS if we have time. feel free to interrupt.
[01:05] Mark: Quick ask up front - we need confirmation about data residency for PHI-adjacent metadata; does Redwood support EU and US dedicated zones?
[01:28] Jordan: yes, we offer hosted plus dedicated and private deployments; for strict residency we'd recommend Dedicated or Private - you can pin region, and we can enforce egress rules. we'll show a doc link after.
[01:55] Ravi: Also need to understand audit log retention periods and whether logs can stream to our SIEM (we use Splunk).
[02:08] Sam: short answer: yes. we support streaming audit logs via secure syslog/S3 forwarders and have sample parsers for Splunk. retention varies by plan, but we can configure long-term storage for Dedicated.
[02:38] Aisha: ok, let's start with the SOC 2 / ISO stuff - do you have a current Type II report and ISO cert we can download? procurement will ask for them.
[02:52] Priya: we do. we host redacted copies in the Redwood Trust Center. jordan will share a link and we can set up a service account/temporary access for your audit team. small caveat: some raw evidence is internal and redacted, but control mappings and test results are available.
[03:20] Jordan: i'll drop the shareable link after this call, and include instructions for requesting access for auditors.
[03:40] Jenna: when you say redacted, what gets redacted? like, user ids or IP addresses?
[03:49] Priya: typically PII or customer-identifiable info - things that would normally be redacted in third-party reports. control evidence names and test procedures are visible. we can produce targeted artifacts on NDA.
[04:12] Aisha: good. we need a controls mapping - our internal control ids mapped to your controls for the SOC 2/ISO family. can you provide that?
[04:23] Priya: yes - we have a spreadsheet that maps Redwood controls to SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria and the ISO 27001 Annex A controls. we'll populate with suggested mapping to sentinel controls but we'll need your help to finalize mapping to your ids.
[04:40] Jordan: action: priya will send that spreadsheet and guidance on how to review.
[04:50] Mark: switching to identity - SSO is a must. we run Okta with SAML and SCIM for provisioning. how's SSO and RBAC supported?
[05:03] Sam: we support SAML SSO, OIDC, and SCIM provisioning for users/groups. RBAC has role tiers (admin, dev, reader) and you can map SAML groups to those roles. for service accounts we recommend short-lived keys via STS and strict scopes.
[05:32] Ravi: Do you support enforced MFA and logging for privileged actions?
[05:39] Priya: enforcing MFA is done at the IdP level - Okta can require MFA. we log privileged actions to audit logs, including role changes and key creation. those logs are immutable and can be exported.
[06:02] Jenna: about service accounts - can they be restricted by CIDR or VPC peering only? we want to limit access to our internal networks.
[06:15] Sam: yes for Dedicated/private you can set VPC peering and restrict API access to your CIDR ranges. Hosted can allow IP allowlists per account but for strict network isolation Dedicated/Private is the recommended path.
[06:45] Aisha: encryption - what's at-rest encryption, keys, BYOK? do you use KMS or HSM?
[06:55] Priya: at-rest encryption uses AES-256; by default keys are managed by Redwood KMS (cloud KMS for hosted), but we support BYOK with customer-managed KMS keys in AWS KMS and HSM integrations for Private deployments. for Dedicated we can do customer KMS as well; we'll go into specifics in the KMS deep-dive.
[07:30] Mark: do you support key rotation and separation of duties for key management?
[07:36] Sam: key rotation is supported; you can configure rotation policies and we log every key operation. separation of duties is accomplished via RBAC + KMS policies; HSM setups can enforce stricter controls.
[07:58] Ravi: audit logs and retention - what's the default retention and what are options for 7 years? we need some artifacts showing immutable logs for audits.
[08:12] Priya: default for hosted is 90 days but we can configure longer retention on Dedicated and Private. for long-term retention we export to your long-term S3 or archival storage; the audit trails remain verifiable via signed hashes. we'll include a doc with examples.
[08:42] Aisha: great - regarding SIEM integration we need schema examples for Splunk mapping so our SOC team can onboard logs quickly.
[08:52] Sam: we'll attach Splunk sample queries and field mappings; we have a Splunk app customers typically use.
[09:15] Jordan: i'd like to surface one common confusion - people expect raw transcripts and KV cache to be stored, but Redwood's runtime keeps ephemeral caches per request and the default retention for request payloads depends on account settings; for compliance customers we can disable retention or enforce short TTLs.
[09:45] Jenna: whats the default TTL for request logs?
[09:49] Priya: default is 30 days for hosted telemetry; request payloads can be turned off and token-level data redaction is supported on Dedicated.
[10:05] Mark: about evidence for SOC 2 - procurement will request full set of control test results. will you provide mapping to our control ids?
[10:16] Priya: we'll share the mapping spreadsheet and a redacted report; for full unredacted evidence we require an NDA and auditor-specific access.
[10:30] Aisha: how do you handle subprocessor disclosures and vendor attestations? we need a list of subprocessors and dates of last review.
[10:40] Jordan: Trust Center includes a subprocessors page with current list and last audit dates. for Dedicated customers we can provide extended documentation and supply chain attestations on request.
[11:00] Ravi: curious about FedRAMP or HIPAA-specific controls - our healthcare customers require this posture. do you have HIPAA BAAs?
[11:10] Sam: Redwood offers HIPAA support via Dedicated/Private; we have BAAs for qualifying deployments. hosted can be configured but typically we recommend Dedicated for PHI, and we can sign a BAA for certain enterprise agreements.
[11:32] Mark: any SOC2 exclusions or open exceptions we should know?
[11:37] Priya: no open exceptions in the current Type II; the report notes a small administrative finding from earlier in the year around onboard docs which was remediated. we'll flag that in the notes.
[11:58] Jenna: technical - network path for logs to SIEM; do you push or do we pull?
[12:04] Sam: both: we can push to your S3 or syslog endpoint via encrypted channels, or you can pull from S3 using IAM roles. push uses mTLS or S3 SSE.
[12:30] Aisha: about Trust Center access - how do we provision auditor access that is timeboxed?
[12:37] Jordan: we create a time-limited service account with read-only scopes and you can request it via the Trust Center request workflow. we also support emailing an artifact bundle for auditors.
[12:55] Mark: does Trust Center support control-by-control evidence download or only PDF reports?
[13:00] Priya: you can export control-by-control evidence and the mapping spreadsheets. some raw logs are not directly downloadable but can be provided under NDA.
[13:25] Ravi: ok let's go deeper on KMS and BYOK - for us we need HSM-backed keys and separation for encryption key custody. how would that work?
[13:36] Sam: for Private deployments we can set up an HSM cluster (customer-managed) and integrate via PKCS#11 or CloudHSM; keys never leave the HSM. for AWS KMS we can do custom key policies and restrict key usage to specific Redwood roles.
[14:05] Jenna: do you support envelope encryption so data keys rotate without re-encrypting entire data stores?
[14:11] Priya: yes we use envelope encryption patterns; the per-record data key is wrapped by a KMS key, enabling rotation without full reencrypt.
[14:35] Aisha: are key operations logged in immutable audit trails tied to identity?
[14:40] Sam: yes, KMS operations are logged with actor identity and included in audit logs. for HSM we produce additional attestation logs.
[15:02] Jordan: switching to deployment options quick run-through: Hosted is fastest but less isolated; Dedicated gives you reserved capacity, network isolation, and longer retention; Private gives you full control and on-prem options.
[15:25] Mark: for procurement - do you have standard contract language for data residency and egress restrictions?
[15:31] Jordan: yes, we have addendum language - we'll attach sample DPA clauses and regional data residency terms.
[15:50] Ravi: show me a typical controls mapping example - how does an ISO control map to your runtime controls?
[15:59] Priya: (screen share) for example ISO A.12.4 (logging) maps to our Audit Logging control: immutable log store, export options, SIEM integrations, log integrity checks. we'll populate specifics in the spreadsheet.
[16:25] Aisha: one operational ask - during an audit, can you provide export of user activity for a given period, with redaction options?
[16:36] Sam: yes, exports are possible; we support filters by user, action, time range. redaction is applied to PII fields by default unless you request full data under NDA.
[16:58] Mark: any third-party pentest cadence we can review?
[17:04] Priya: annual third-party pentests plus continuous vuln scanning; we publish summary findings in the Trust Center and full reports under NDA.
[17:26] Jenna: about SAML group sync - if a group mapping changes do role changes take effect immediately? what's the consistency model?
[17:34] Sam: group changes via SCIM are near real-time; SAML assertion-based role mapping applies at login. SCIM provisioning updates are typically within seconds to a minute.
[17:58] Ravi: compliance requests often want to know about encryption key compromise procedures - do you have documented playbooks?
[18:07] Priya: yes we maintain incident response runbooks including key compromise, with roles and notification timelines; we'll share an exec summary.
[18:28] Aisha: any SOC2 exceptions around subprocessors or outages last year?
[18:35] Jordan: no service-impacting outages in the reporting period; subprocessors are listed and the trust center shows dates of attestations.
[18:55] Mark: curious about how you handle model weights and caching for inference - are model artifacts considered customer data?
[19:04] Sam: model weights are part of the hosting environment; customer prompts and generated outputs are treated as customer data. KV caches are ephemeral; we can configure not to persist them.
[19:28] Priya: and for customers with strict requirements we offer Dedicated with pinned model variants and no shared caches.
[19:45] Jenna: for logging, is there a way to separate metadata from content so we can keep content off-site?
[19:52] Priya: yes you can disable content retention or configure content to go to your own S3, while metadata and telemetry remain in Redwood for observability.
[20:10] Aisha: ok, next steps and timeline - we need the controls mapping and the SOC2 artifacts by next tuesday for our compliance intake.
[20:20] Jordan: understood, we'll get the Trust Center link over today and priya will send the spreadsheet by Tuesday.
[20:32] Ravi: follow-up deep-dive on KMS - we want that the week after next, any day except Thursday.
[20:40] Priya: i'll send avail slots in the next 24 hours.
[21:00] Mark: quick procurement Q: Dedicated pricing and contract said in RFP - can you provide a sample SLA and data residency addendum?
[21:10] Jordan: yes will include with the pricing outline.
[21:30] Aisha: one more question - for auditors wanting direct log access, can you enable temporary read-only S3 buckets with object-level logging?
[21:38] Sam: yes, we can provide time-limited S3 access or signed artifact bundles; both are common.
[21:55] Jenna: technical nit - do you sign exports with hash or have tamper-evidence?
[22:02] Priya: exports include signed manifests and hashes for integrity verification.
[22:25] Jordan: any other open risks or questions?
[22:30] Aisha: nothing else from me, this covers most of procurement's checklist.
[22:36] Mark: same, we'll wait on the mapping and Trust Center link.
[22:42] Ravi: thanks all.
[22:50] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.

(rough transcript continues with clarifications and short Q&A, timestamps approximate)
